I also wrote and executed a separate standard-library-only reference audit that reconstructs the geometry, checks the complete matchings, independently identifies paid edges, and performs additional path/pair and small-grid enumeration.This review concerns the supplied archive. Its embedded git-archive comment is d018eaab754c0266ec5742dc1c32e0b781f43093; I did not fetch GitHub or independently authenticate that remote commit.1. General theorem: the conservation and eligibility arguments are correctHypotheses and prerequisite interfacesI inspected the relevant interfaces in all three prerequisite notes: the exposure and normal-form construction, the physical capacity-one path representation, the canonical exterior barrier, and the fixed-path completion criterion. I did not treat their earlier review verdicts as validation of this theorem.The new argument retains the hypotheses it needs: a full perfect auxiliary matching; white selected terminals; separated internally matched cores; centre-neighbour localization; exactly  $r-1$  white HH sources; a  $W$ -saturating  $\Gamma$ -matching; the surplus-one exterior matching; H6; and finite nonnegative actual-edge weights. It does not assume  $J=I$ .    MULTICENTRE_HALL_BALANCEIn particular, the inherited conclusions used here are
$$N_T(D)=F,\qquad |D|=|F|,$$
and the exact restricted normal-form value
$$U_1=\min_{j\in J}\sigma_j.$$
The latter is not being promoted to an unrestricted optimization formula.The global HH budget counts each source exactly onceFor a fixed full  $N$ , use the tagged union of  $M$  and  $N$ , retaining doubled edges as two differently tagged incidences. Each  $P$ -vertex has degree two and each  $Q$ -vertex degree one. Consequently, its terminal components are alternating paths with one more  $N$ -edge than  $M$ -edges. Their endpoints have opposite checkerboard colours.Thus the terminal paths induce a bijection
$$T\sqcup W\longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{black}}.$$
If  $k$  centres are TH endpoints, precisely  $r-k$  centres are HH endpoints. They consume precisely  $r-k$  distinct members of  $W$ . Hence
$$\#\{\text{exterior HH paths}\}
=|W|-(r-k)
=(r-1)-(r-k)
=k-1.$$
This also gives  $k\ge1$ .Independently, counting the endpoints in  $D$  gives
$$|D|=(|F|-a)+b+c.$$
Since  $|D|=|F|$ ,
$$a=b+c.$$
Because every HH path counted by  $c$  is exterior,
$$0\le c\le k-1.$$
When all  $k$  TH-centre sources lie in  $F$ , those  $k$  distinct sources all terminate outside  $D$ , so
$$a\ge k,\qquad b=a-c\ge k-(k-1)=1.$$
There is no per-centre reuse of an HH source in this calculation. It works for arbitrary  $k$ , not just one or two centres. Moreover, an  $E$ -to- $D$  path cannot be direct, because  $D$  has no direct neighbour in  $E$ . The supplied proof establishes exactly these conclusions.    MULTICENTRE_HALL_BALANCEThe matching augmentation conclusion is valid—but only in the stated senseThe HH-centre components of the original  $N$  induce a partial matching in  $\Gamma$ . Their sources and centres are distinct. Core separation and centre-neighbour localization ensure that a non-direct path reaching a centre has its interior in that centre’s core.Since  $\Gamma$  admits a  $W$ -saturating matching, this partial matching can be augmented to one. An augmenting path preserves the set of already matched right vertices, while adding one previously unmatched right vertex. Therefore every originally HH-matched centre remains matched on the right.The unique centre omitted by the final saturating matching was consequently an original TH centre. By definition, it belongs to  $J$ . This proves that the original  $N$  contains at least one eligible TH centre.    MULTICENTRE_HALL_BALANCETwo distinctions matter:The augmentation need not preserve the original matching edges.It is not asserted to reroute the original physical HH paths inside the same  $N$ .Neither stronger claim is needed. Augmentation is used only to identify an eligible centre among the TH centres already present.The three-way case split is exhaustiveFor any full  $N$ , the cases are:SituationWitness obtainedLower bound on  $f(N)$ An eligible TH centre has its source in  $E$ Its individual centre path $U_1$ No such centre exists, but an ineligible TH centre has its source in  $E$ That path and an eligible TH-centre path from  $F$  $F_X$ Neither preceding case occursAn eligible TH-centre path from  $F$ , and the forced  $E$ -to- $D$  path $F_H$ In the second case, the eligible-centre lemma supplies the required eligible TH centre, whose source must lie in  $F$ . In the third case, all TH-centre sources lie in  $F$ , so the global balance argument applies.The selected components are vertex-disjoint because they are distinct components of the same tagged union. H6 makes the centre paths nontrivial; the defining property of  $D$  makes the compensation path nontrivial. Nonnegative weights justify discarding all other TH expenses. This proves the minimum of the three bounds.    MULTICENTRE_HALL_BALANCEThe  $\Lambda$  step is also consistent with the new eligibility argument. Using the inherited identity
$$\Lambda=\min_{j\in J}\rho_j,$$
an eligible TH-centre path in  $N$  has expense at least  $\rho_j\ge\Lambda$ . Thus the maximum with  $\Lambda$  is justified without any assumption that every root is eligible.Finally, every  $F_X$ -feasible pair is  $F_{CC}$ -feasible after forgetting the extra quotas. Therefore
$$F_X\ge F_{CC}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
B_M\ge B_H.$$
When  $C_-=\varnothing$ ,  $F_X=+\infty$ , giving the advertised all-roots-eligible specialization.2. Physical capacities, cross pairing, zero weights, and infinityI found no duplicated-capacity or labelled-demand error in the flow construction.There is one capacity-one actual arc for each physical  $M$ -edge, directed black-to-white. It is the unique outgoing grid arc at its black  $P$ -endpoint and the unique incoming grid arc at its white  $P$ -endpoint. Its capacity therefore protects both physical endpoints. The source and terminal capacities protect  $Q$ -endpoints, while the collectors enforce the source-group and sink-group quotas.Crucially, the collectors do not prescribe which source group reaches which sink group. Both  $F_H$  and  $F_X$  are unlabelled two-unit flows. This matches their definitions and permits cross pairing. The new note explicitly retains this convention.    MULTICENTRE_HALL_BALANCENonnegative-cost circulations can be discarded without increasing expense; at a minimum any retained circulation has zero cost. Negative reverse residual costs represent cancellation, not an additional copy of a physical resource.Zero weights do not invalidate the theorem. Nontrivial means “contains an actual edge,” not “has positive expense.” The proof uses nonnegativity, not strict positivity. The  $F_{CC}\ge2$  and  $F_H\ge K+1$  assertions belong to the separate positive-weight example, where their positivity assumptions hold.Infinite relaxation values are handled correctly. A case that actually occurs supplies a finite physical witness for its associated term. An infeasible branch can therefore be represented by  $+\infty$  without breaking the case argument. In the implementation, None is used for infeasibility, rather than a large finite sentinel; finite zero values are not discarded.The  $O(v^2)$  arithmetic-time and  $O(v)$ -stored-word claims are consistent with bounded grid degree, a constant number of value-two flow computations, and the inherited matching procedures. They are not bit-complexity claims for arbitrarily large integer weights.3. The canonical two-cheap-edge all- $K$  family checks outI independently reconstructed the  $18\times18$  board and canonical matching from the five origins and the displayed local pairing rule. The reconstructed  $M$ , cores, centres, and selected set agree with the coordinate certificate.This is indeed the canonical matching with two cheap edges, not the predecessor’s changed matching with three cheap edges.The first-actual-edge argument proves the lower bound for every  $K$ The cheap actual edges have black endpoints  $(2,2)$  and  $(6,8)$ . Their selected neighbours are exactly
$$N((2,2))\cap T=\{(1,2)\},\qquad
N((6,8))\cap T=\{(5,8)\}.$$
Both selected neighbours lie in  $F$ ; all other neighbours of those black endpoints lie in  $P$ .A nontrivial path starting in  $E$  first traverses an auxiliary edge to a black  $P$ -vertex and then its actual matching edge. That first actual edge cannot be cheap. Therefore every such path already incurs cost  $K$  at its first actual edge.It follows that
$$U_1\ge K,\qquad F_H\ge K+1.$$
The second inequality remains valid under cross pairing: an  $F_H$ -pair always has an  $E$ -source path costing at least  $K$  and another nontrivial, physically disjoint path costing at least one. This is the correct all- $K$  argument, not extrapolation from the five numerical samples.    MULTICENTRE_HALL_BALANCEThe upper witnesses have the claimed symbolic coefficientsFor the optimal full matching, my independent tagged-component reconstruction found exactly one paid actual edge:
$$\{(8,6),(8,7)\}.$$
Thus its paid-edge coefficient vector, ordered as
$$(\text{number of cheap edges},\text{number of other edges}),$$
is exactly  $(0,1)$ . The fixed full matching therefore has expense  $K$  for every  $K\ge3$ .The displayed paths  $A,R$  are physically disjoint and attain  $F_H$  with coefficient vector  $(1,1)$ , giving  $F_H\le K+1$ . The two cheap centre paths  $A,B$  attain  $F_{CC}=2$ . I also independently confirmed
$$\rho=(1,1,K,K,K),\qquad J=I.$$
Combining these facts gives
$$\boxed{
B_H=2,\qquad B_M=f^*=U_1=K,\qquad F_H=K+1,\qquad F_X=+\infty
}$$
for every integer  $K\ge3$ . The fixed matching supplies the upper bound, while the theorem supplies the matching lower bound.
